Honda Motor (NYSE:HMC) Downgraded by Wall Street Zen to Hold
sum: - Wall Street Zen downgraded Honda Motor from “buy” to “hold.” Despite that move, MarketBeat reports an overall “Moderate Buy” consensus and a $34 average price target.
- Honda reported quarterly EPS of $0.32, below the $0.95 analyst consensus, while revenue of $39.13 billion exceeded estimates of $36.68 billion.
- Shares opened at $34.33, up 2.4%; the stock’s 52-week range is $23.25 to $36.88.
Honda Motor (NYSE:HMC - Get Free Report) was downgraded by equities researchers at Wall Street Zen from a "buy" rating to a "hold" rating in a report released on Saturday, Wall Street Zen reports.

A number of other equities research analysts also recently weighed in on HMC. Zacks Research raised Honda Motor from a "hold" rating to a "strong-buy" rating in a research note on Monday, August 17th. BNP Paribas Exane began coverage on Honda Motor in a research note on Friday, September 18th. They issued a "neutral" rating and a $34.00 price target for the company. Finally, Weiss Ratings upgraded Honda Motor from a "sell (d)" rating to a "sell (d+)" rating in a report on Thursday, October 22nd. Two analysts have rated the stock with a Strong Buy rating, two have issued a Hold rating and one has issued a Sell rating to the stock. According to MarketBeat.com, Honda Motor presently has an average rating of "Moderate Buy" and a consensus target price of $34.00.

Shares of NYSE:HMC opened at $34.33 on Friday. The company has a current ratio of 1.32, a quick ratio of 1.04 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.73. Honda Motor has a 1 year low of $23.25 and a 1 year high of $36.88. The business has a fifty day simple moving average of $33.19 and a 200 day simple moving average of $29.15.

Honda Motor (NYSE:HMC - Get Free Report) last released its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, November 10th. The company reported $0.32 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, missing analysts' consensus estimates of $0.95 by ($0.63). Honda Motor had a negative net margin of 0.97% and a negative return on equity of 1.78%. The firm had revenue of $39.13 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $36.68 billion. On average, equities research analysts expect that Honda Motor will post 2.42 EPS for the current fiscal year.

Honda After H1'27 Earnings: Buy, Hold or Sell the Stock Now?
sum: Japanese auto giant Honda Motor HMC reported a strong first half of fiscal 2027. Sales revenues rose 13.2% to ¥12.04 trillion, and operating profit jumped 48.1% to ¥648.7 billion. Net profit attributable to owners climbed 65.7% to ¥516.8 billion, even after the company absorbed ¥484.8 billion of EV-related losses.

Riding on strong first-half results, management raised its full-year operating profit forecast by ¥130 billion to ¥780 billion. It now expects net profit of ¥500 billion, a sharp turnaround from the ¥424 billion loss in fiscal 2026. With the recovery gathering pace, is HMC stock worth buying now? Let’s dig deeper.

The EV charges grabbed the headlines, but the core business tells a better story. Adjusted operating profit in the automobile segment, which excludes EV-related losses, surged 217.9% to ¥479 billion. The adjusted margin expanded to 6.2% from 2.2%. Higher North American volumes, favorable currency movements and tighter expense control all contributed.

Tariff-related gains of ¥97 billion also helped, partly through one-time refunds. Honda expects total EV-related losses of ¥520 billion this year. Since ¥484.8 billion has already been booked, only about ¥35 billion is left for the second half, which suggests the heaviest part of the clean-up is behind it.

Demand for fuel-efficient vehicles is lifting the whole industry. Honda’s closest peer, Toyota’s TM hybrid sales rose 8.3% to 2.45 million units in the first half, and Honda is riding the same wave. Its global hybrid retail sales rose to 494,000 units from 454,000 a year ago. Excluding China, they climbed to 476,000 from 422,000, a gain of nearly 13%.

Honda is also building for the next leg of growth. A new Ohio plant will lift North American capacity from 1.67 million to 1.91 million units by 2029. From that year, the company plans to introduce larger hybrids in the D-segment and above. This extends the hybrid opportunity beyond today’s lineup.

Honda’s two-wheeler franchise remains its profit anchor. Motorcycle sales rose 10.6% to a record 11.9 million units, led by India and Brazil. Operating profit grew 19.2% to ¥439 billion at a margin of 19.3% in the first half of fiscal 2027. That single segment generated about two-thirds of group operating profit.

Activa no longer enough: Honda broadens scooter strategy as rivals close in
sum: Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India (HMSI) is looking beyond its flagship Activa as changing consumer preferences and growing competition force the company to broaden its scooter portfolio.

Honda's share of India's 8.1 million-unit scooter market fell from 57% in FY17 to 39% in FY26, while TVS Motor Company's share rose from 15% to 28% and Suzuki Motorcycle India's share increased from 5% to 14%, according to data shared by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers.

The Activa has been central to Honda's scooter business for more than two decades, built around family buyers, customer trust and word-of-mouth recommendations. Honda now sees an opportunity to add products for customers with different preferences, particularly younger buyers who increasingly research products and global models online.

“The Activa has been very successful in the past because of word-of-mouth recommendations, customer trust and its reputation for good quality,” Tsutsumu Otani, president and chief executive officer of HMSI, told Moneycontrol in an interaction on October 31.

“However, the way information is communicated has changed. It is no longer just word of mouth. The internet and social media have become important, particularly because Generation Z (Gen Z) consumers check information about products and models globally,” he said.

Honda's strategy is already moving beyond the traditional family scooter. The company recently introduced the ADV160, made in India, as part of its plan to expand its range of global models in the country.
Priced at around Rs 1.7 lakh, the ADV160 costs more than twice the Activa and is aimed at customers looking for a different product proposition.

Honda to spend $3 billion on new hybrid car plant in Ohio
sum: Honda Motor Co. plans to build a $3 billion factory in central Ohio to manufacture its next-generation hybrids, boosting its output capacity for the popular vehicles.

The Japanese automaker announced on Monday the new plant will start production in 2029 and expand its output by 240,000 vehicles a year. Honda has been mulling over the decision for months as part of a strategic pivot earlier this year away from all-electric vehicles. It aims to introduce 15 new hybrids globally by March 2030, primarily targeting North America.

“This is not simply an investment in another plant,” Bob Nelson, executive vice president of the company’s US business operations, said at a press conference. “It is an investment in the future of Honda Manufacturing in America.”

Honda’s US sales have risen 5% in the first 10 months of the year, powered by strong demand for hybrid versions of its best-selling CR-V compact SUV, Accord mid-sized sedan and compact Civic sedan. Fuel-efficient hybrids, which make up about a third of the company’s total sales volume in the US, have caught on with cost-conscious buyers as gas prices have soared.
Honda is preparing to introduce a new system that will provide hybrid options for its larger, V6 engine-powered vehicles such as the Pilot SUV and upscale Acura MDX SUV.

The new facility will be located between two existing auto assembly plants it operates in Ohio. It will be tooled to build gas-only, hybrid and fully electric vehicles, but the company didn’t provide a breakdown by production volume.
Honda also wouldn’t say which vehicles will be made in the new plant, but its focus will be on boosting output of models offering a hybrid option, including all-new models.

Honda Invests CAD 166 Million to Upgrade Canadian Production for Next-Generation Models
sum: (AWP Alliance News) - Honda will invest CAD 166 million to upgrade its Ontario manufacturing operations for next-generation hybrid and internal combustion models, according to a Nov. 9, 2026, announcement. The project will modernize facilities and introduce production technology to meet growing North American demand for hybrids.

Including this investment, planned spending and related costs total CAD 867 million to improve manufacturing quality, efficiency and production flexibility. Upgrades at U.S. plants will also support a North American production network for next-generation models.
The investment supports a plan announced in May 2026 to launch 15 next-generation hybrid models globally by fiscal 2029, with North America a priority market.

Makino Gives Kunimitsu Honda Critical Pole for Finale
sum: Honda driver Tadasuke Makino gave Team Kunimitsu a crucial pole position for Sunday’s final round of the SUPER GT season at Motegi, as the two main title contenders ended up sharing the front row for the title-deciding 250km race.

Makino left it until the very end of the 15-minute GT500 session to post his best lap of 1:36.135, putting the No. 100 Honda HRC Prelude-GT he shares with Naoki Yamamoto 0.278 seconds ahead of Kenta Yamashita’s No. 36 TOM’S Toyota GR Supra.

Kunimitsu duo Makino and Yamamoto took over the lead of the standings with a provisional fifth-place finish in the first race, and pole gives them a three-point cushion over main rivals Yamashita and Sho Tsuboi, who could only finish 10th on Saturday.
A win for either of the two cars starting on the front row would be enough to win the championship no matter what happens to the other.

While Honda scored a sixth consecutive GT500 pole, the car responsible for the last three of them, the Dunlop-shod Nakajima Racing car, was third-fastest this time around in the hands of Riki Okusa, 0.323 seconds off the pace of Makino.
Yuto Nomura (Real Racing) and Kakunoshin Ohta (ARTA No. 8) made it four Hondas locking out the top five places on the grid.

Nirei Fukuzumi was sixth-fastest in the Rookie Racing Toyota that was disqualified (provisionally pending appeal) from second place in the opening race, ahead of the best of the Nissan Z NISMOs, the works No. 23 machine of Katsumasa Chiyo.

QuantumScape shares rise 6% as stock tests key moving average resistance
sum: QuantumScape Corp shares gained over 6% on Thursday, yet remain below key moving averages as the stock tests technical resistance. A new joint research program with Honda aims to expand solid-state battery applications beyond EVs to motorcycles and industrial equipment. Analysts maintain a Hold rating ahead of the July 22, 2026 earnings report, where a loss of 18 cents per share is expected.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

QuantumScape Corp shares rose 6.03% to $7.03 on Thursday as traders leaned into higher-beta names and risk appetite remained firm. The stock is attempting a rebound but continues to face significant technical resistance, trading below key moving averages that suggest the broader trend remains pressured.

Despite Thursday's bounce, QuantumScape is trading below its critical moving averages. The stock is 2.9% below the 20-day SMA ($7.22), 9.2% below the 50-day SMA ($7.71), and 29.4% below the 200-day SMA ($9.93). This technical structure follows a "death cross" in February, where the 50-day SMA fell below the 200-day SMA.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands at 45.01, indicating neutral territory. This level suggests the stock is neither overbought nor oversold, often aligning with choppy rebounds that require follow-through above resistance to establish a new trend.

Traders are watching specific price levels for direction. Key resistance is identified at $7.50, a round-number area near the 50-day EMA ($7.52). On the downside, key support sits at $6.50, a level that has recently acted as a buying zone above the 52-week low of $5.90.

In late June, QuantumScape and Honda announced a joint research program focused on solid-state battery development and related manufacturing processes. This partnership expands QuantumScape's platform technology narrative beyond passenger electric vehicle battery packs.

Toyota Surges Post Q2 Earnings: Is the Stock Worth Buying Now?
sum: Toyota TM shares rose more than 9% yesterday following its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results, taking its monthly gains to roughly 20%, outperforming the industry and its peers Honda HMC and Nissan NSANY. While Honda shares gained 14.5% over the past month, Nissan stock fell roughly 2%.

The rally may appear surprising at first glance, considering the automaker reported an 18.5% year-over-year decline in net income to ¥759.4 billion in second-quarter fiscal 2027. However, investors focused on two more encouraging developments — a stronger full-year profit outlook and an expanded shareholder-return program.

Toyota's latest results suggest that its operating business is performing better than its bottom line indicates. Meanwhile, its hybrid-focused strategy, improving North American profitability and higher shareholder payouts offer reasons for optimism. But with the stock having rallied sharply, is TM still worth buying? Let's dig deeper.
Toyota Motor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Toyota Motor Corporation Quote

The decline in net income does not fully capture the improvement in Toyota's operations. The decline came from foreign-exchange losses and higher finance costs, which together outweighed an improvement in operating profit. Operating income grew 34% during the quarter under review.

The automotive division, Toyota's core, saw revenues rise 8.2% to ¥11.96 trillion. Its operating profit jumped 53% to ¥878.2 billion, helped by favorable currency movements, pricing actions and lower expenses, though higher material costs took a bite. The smaller "All Other" businesses also did well, with revenues up 19.6% and operating profit up 51% to ¥47.3 billion.
Financial services was the soft spot. Revenues rose 14% to ¥1.36 trillion, but operating income fell 13.8% to ¥196.7 billion. It is a modest drag next to the strength in autos.

Egypt Raises Over $650m In IPO Of State-Owned Bank
sum: Egypt on Monday raised more than $650 million in its initial public offering of the state-owned Banque du Caire, marking one of the biggest asset sales in years as international lenders push a privatisation drive.
The offering comes as Egypt advances reforms under an International Monetary Fund programme aimed at boosting private sector participation and reducing the state’s role in the economy.
The government has previously said it plans to sell stakes in over 30 state-owned companies under commitments linked to its IMF support programme.
The bank’s majority shareholder, Banque Misr, sold 6.86 billion shares, representing 45 percent of Banque du Caire, at 5.30 Egyptian pounds per share, according to the final offer announcement.
The sale raised about 36.37 billion pounds ($658 million) and valued the lender at around 80.83 billion pounds ($1.46 billion).
In June, authorities granted preliminary listings to four state-owned companies ahead of planned stock market offerings by May 2027.

Prime Minister Moustafa Madbouly said Monday’s listing came despite regional tensions and underscored the government’s commitment to “continuing its programme of state asset offerings, aiming to unlock greater value from public assets”.

Petrol Cars Lose No.1 Spot in India – CNG, Hybrid & EVs Together Take 42% Share
sum: India’s passenger-vehicle market has crossed an important milestone. For the first time, alternative-fuel passenger vehicles collectively outsold petrol-powered cars in a single month.
According to FADA’s August 2026 retail data, CNG/LPG, hybrids and EVs together accounted for 41.95% of passenger-vehicle registrations, marginally ahead of petrol/ethanol at 40.85%.
This is significant because India’s transition away from conventional petrol cars is not being driven by EVs alone. Instead, CNG, hybrids and electric cars are all contributing to the shift.
A year earlier, petrol/ethanol still accounted for 46.89% of passenger-vehicle retail, while CNG/LPG stood at 21.47%, hybrids at 8.13% and EVs at 5.38%.
That means petrol has lost roughly 6 percentage points of share in one year, while all three major alternative-powertrain categories have strengthened.
CNG/LPG remains by far the largest alternative-fuel category, accounting for 25.28% of passenger-vehicle sales in August.
That means roughly one in four cars registered in India now runs on CNG/LPG.

Honda officially reveals new CB1000F in three colour options
sum: After revealing the CB1000F as a concept during the prestigious Suzuka 8 Hour race in August, Honda has now revealed the finished product.
The new model arrives in three equally classy colourways, as well as sharing many similarities to the recently launched CB1000 Hornet.

According to Honda, the three paint schemes are called Wolf Silver Metallic with Blue Stripe, Wolf Silver Metallic with Grey Stripe and Graphite Black. The new model is expected to arrive in UK dealers in early 2026.

Now onto the bike itself, as the CB1000F is the latest model in what is a 65-year history for the CB family. Delving back into the archives, the new model specifically harps back to the 1980s, taking after the CB750F in its appearance.
That bike is one that racing fans from that era might remember well, as it powered American rider Freddie Spencer’s AMA Championship campaigns.

As I mentioned above, the CB1000 Hornet is an important bike to think of when looking at the new CB1000F, and that’s because the two bikes share many core components, although the latter has had its power output adjusted and moved down the rev range to offer a more relaxed riding experience.

Honda says it has been “developed under the conceptual target of creating the ‘Best Balanced Roadster’. The CB1000F handles like a middleweight but with big bike feel. And, with the ‘80s now proving such an influential decade in clothing, music, style, and more, the CB1000F is very much a bike ready for today.”

Japan's Honda reports robust results after its first ever annual loss
sum: TOKYO (AP) — Honda's profit for the fiscal first quarter more than doubled from a year ago, as the Japanese automaker continues to tackle a turnaround from the first full year loss in its history.
Tokyo-based Honda Motor Co. said Wednesday its April-June profit totaled 456.9 billion yen ($2.9 billion), up from 196.6 billion yen for the same period a year ago.
Quarterly sales rose 13.5% to 6.06 trillion yen ($38 billion), as vehicles sold well in the U.S. and India, according to the maker of the Accord sedan, Fit subcompact and Super Cub motorcycle.

Honda previously recorded a 423.9 billion yen ($2.7 billion) loss for the fiscal year ended in March, acknowledging heavy costs for its electric-vehicle plans, which didn't measure up to the original ambitions, partly because of U.S. President Donald Trump's policies.
Analysts say many consumers weren't ready to go electric. Honda has abandoned many of its plans for EV models.

The Trump administration has pulled back on incentive programs for EVs and withheld money to states wanting to add more EV charging stations, even as gas prices have soared over the war in Iran. Trump's tariffs on imported autos and auto parts, lowered to 15% from the initial 25%, also worked to dent Honda's profitability.
For the latest quarter, Honda's motorcycle operations were highly lucrative with sales going strong in Brazil and India. Car sales grew in Japan and the U.S., while struggling in China.

Disabled motorcyclist continues remarkable two-wheel journey at 75 years of age
sum: Max Jones, a long-time motorcyclist from Pembrokeshire, Wales, is continuing to ride bikes despite suffering from severe arthritis at the age of 75, and he does so by riding a Honda Gold Wing trike that features an attached trailer for his wheelchair.
Jones is a former police officer who has been riding motorcycles since the 1970s, and has completed trips to Ireland, Scotland and throughout Europe.

But due to his arthritis, Jones has had to change the way he goes riding, which includes transitioning from two wheels to three. When he’s not riding to his destinations, Jones also relies on the use of his four-wheel WHILL C2 powerchair, which is mounted inside his trailer for any trip he takes aboard his Gold Wing trike.

Jones served the police force for 27 years as a Constable, and later as a Sergeant. His roles were occupied across various areas of South Wales, while the 75-year-old also spent two years as a Law Instructor at the Welsh Police Training Centre.
Speaking about his journey to this point, along with the need to find a wheelchair that could support his current wishes to continuing riding, Jones said:

"If you start looking for a manual wheelchair when you are tall and 17 stone like me, you have a problem finding anything that will fit. And my wife was going to have to push me around which wouldn't be fair. You need something that will self-propel. I tried loads and, in the end, I believe the powered WHILL range is the best.

“You can't beat it; nothing compares to it. So comfortable. My grandad used to say: 'There's nothing more expensive than buying cheap'. Honda delays takeover of Astemo
sum: Honda Motor has announced that it has delayed plans to make local automotive systems manufacturer Astemo Ltd a consolidated subsidiary. The Japanese automaker confirmed that it now expects to complete the acquisition of a majority stake in Astemo by the end of 2026, instead of by the end of the second quarter as it had originally announced in December 2025.

Honda currently holds a 40% stake in Astemo, with Japanese multinational company Hitachi Ltd also holding a 40% stake and JIC Capital (Japanese Investment Corporation) the holding the remaining 20%. Honda has agreed to acquire an additional 21% stake in Astemo from Hitachi, which would lift its holding in the company to 61%.

Astemo produces a wide range of automotive systems, including hardware and software for chassis and powertrain systems, as well as autonomous driving/advanced driver assistance (ADAS) systems, and is central to Honda's plans to develop and produce software-defined vehicles (SDVs) and improve its competitiveness.

Honda said in a statement: "In the face of the rapid and intense changes in the automotive business environment, it is essential for Honda, as a parent company, to lead the transformation of Astemo so that Astemo can pursue the establishment of a business structure that enables high-speed, high-efficiency development of AI and software technologies, which will become increasingly necessary in the era of SDVs. Based on this belief, Honda, Hitachi and JIC Capital agreed in December 2025, that Honda will acquire additional shares of Astemo, equivalent to 21% of all outstanding shares, from Hitachi, thereby changing the shareholding structure to 61% Honda, 19% Hitachi, and 20% JIC Capital.

Honda confirmed that since the initial announcement, it has been working to obtain the necessary clearances and approvals, but that delays in the approval process have resulted in the transaction now expected to be completed by the end of the third quarter of the current fiscal year (FY2026), which ends in March 2027.

sum: TVS Motor became India's top two-wheeler maker by total June sales, surpassing Hero MotoCorp and Honda on the back of strong domestic demand and exports

Tamil Nadu-based TVS Motor Company (TVSM), a part of the TVS Venu group, has become India's largest two-wheeler (2W) manufacturer by total sales volume, combining domestic and international business, for the month of June 2026. The company is already the market leader in the electric two-wheeler (e2W) segment.

The company sold 5.65 lakh units globally, taking the top spot ahead of long-standing leaders Hero MotoCorp, which sold 5.41 lakh units, and Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India, which sold 5.28 lakh units. Though the company had achieved a similar feat in the month of December 2025, it is generally a lean month for 2W-makers.

"This is the first time that we have become clear market leaders. Though a similar feat was achieved in December 2025, it is a post-season month where all players reduce their stocks. Even during Covid, TVS had outsmarted Hero and Honda, but that was also not a period which can be seen as normal," said a industry source.

During the month under review, TVS led Hero by 24,000 units and Honda by 37,000 units in total combined volume. Figures are company-reported wholesale dispatch numbers for June 2026. Total volume reflects combined India domestic dispatches and international business (export) dispatches.

Exports were the decisive factor in the company's performance. TVS's international business volume of 1.54 lakh units was 2.9 times the combined export volume of Hero and Honda. "The export volume reflects TVS's deepening presence across international markets, including Africa, Latin America, Asean, and West Asia, positioning it as an increasingly globally diversified two-wheeler manufacturer," said the source.

The result builds on a sustained multi-quarter trend, with TVS posting the fastest volume growth among major OEMs (original equipment manufacturers) through FY26, and steadily narrowing the gap with Hero and Honda, the source added. TVS grew by 47 per cent, far higher than Hero, Honda, and Bajaj during the month.

Honda CEO says Nissan tie-up is near; brands could share ECUs
sum: Back in February 2025, Nissan and Honda ended merger talks after the two companies couldn't come to a mutual agreement. With it, the hopes of seeing Nissan and Honda become the world's fourth-largest automaker became naught.

Despite the merger not happening, it seems both Honda and Nissan did not abandon possible tie-ups entirely. This comes after Honda Motor Corporation CEO Toshihiro Mibe shared that both brands are close to entering a partnership.

During the recent Honda shareholders' meeting, Mibe apologized to stakeholders after the company posted its first-ever annual loss in years. Combined with the brand turning away from their bold EV strategy, some questioned whether Mibe was making the right decisions. However, the CEO quelled fears by stating that they are working with Nissan for a partnership, with some aspect possibly close to an official announcement.

According to a report by Nikkei Asia, Honda, Nissan, and Mitsubishi could share common ECUs across a range of models, which includes hybrids and EVs. The shared ECUs could reach the market sometime in 2029 or 2030, as there are still questions about the development funding and other important aspects of the shared ECU between the brands. However, an agreement between the brands is expected to happen within weeks.

What could stop the deal between the two brands? Well, Nissan is part of the Renault Nissan Mitsubishi Alliance, and Renault still has a 15% voting stake in Nissan. Since Nissan is a publicly traded company, it will need shareholder consent to enter into any deal or partnership with another entity outside the Alliance.

With Honda and Nissan both in precarious financial situations, it seems both brands cannot afford not to have some sort of partnership. The only question now is, will the two brands actually come to an agreement, and will Renault actually let Nissan have a deal with Honda?

Honda shares rise over 7% as investors shrug off first operating loss in nearly 70 years
sum: Shares of Honda Motor rose over 7% on Friday, even after the Japanese automaker posted its first annual operating loss in nearly 70 years.

Honda swung to an operating loss of 414.3 billion yen ($2.61 billion) for the fiscal year ending March, compared to an operating profit of 1.2 trillion yen the year prior. Provisions made for its ailing electric vehicle business and related investments, competition from its Chinese rivals, as well as a U.S. tariff impact of 346.9 billion yen weighed on its earnings.
"The business environment surrounding the Company has been changing rapidly, and the outlook remains uncertain," Honda said in its earnings statement on Thursday.

As part of its efforts to reorganize its EV business, the automaker said it will cancel market launches and development of some EV models initially planned for production in North America. The Japanese automaker said it expects the restructure of its EV business to cost over $9 billion.

Honda also noted that new EV makers have intensified competition in China. "Under such a challenging and competitive environment, the Company has also revised its product launch plans for certain EV models," Honda added.

"We believe the positive share price reaction is driven by the company's guidance for operating and net profit, both of which came in 38% above consensus estimates," said Masahiro Akita, an analyst from Bernstein.
However, Akita said it's uncertain as to whether the guidance has fully priced in possible losses linked to EV investments.

Honda stock jumps despite first-ever loss as guidance tops estimates
sum: Japan's Honda (HMC) posted its first-ever loss in its 70+ year history as a public company following a strategy shift from EVs, which cost it dearly. But a refocused plan to lean into hybrids and upbeat guidance for the year ahead have investors bullish.
Honda said total EV-related losses for the fiscal year ended March 2026 came in 1.579 trillion yen ($10 billion), leading to an operating profit loss of 414.3 billion yen ($2.625 billion).

"Although the automobile business faced a harsh business environment — including higher tariff burdens and lower unit sales due to factors such as semiconductor supply shortages — we implemented company-wide cost reductions as one team, and excluding EV-related losses, we were profitable," the company said in its presentation.

Good news came with Honda's guidance, however. Though EV-related losses in upcoming March 2027 FY will be 500 billion yen ($3.168 billion), the company still sees operating profit at 500 billion yen. This topped Bloomberg consensus estimates of 212.4 billion yen ($1.35 billion), sending Honda's ADR shares listed in New York up over 5%.

In order to better serve North America and its top market, the US, Honda said it plans to roll out 15 new hybrid models by March 2030, primarily in North America, dropping planned EVs and moving toward mixed powertrain vehicles. Honda said by 2029 it would launch "large size hybrid models" in the D-segment, meaning full-size sedans, wagons, and SUVs.
Honda also said on Thursday that it would drop plans to build out an EV battery supply chain in Canada.

Currently, Honda has five vehicles in its US lineup that offer hybrid powertrains. However, these are of the mild hybrid variety, not plug-ins, which offer more range and efficiency. Honda's lone EV is the Prologue, essentially a re-badged Chevrolet Blazer EV, which has sold at deep discounts at dealerships and will end production in December of this year.

For OEMs with multiple-product firepower, it’s often that a single product provides an extra dose of ammo. Like the Jupiter is to TVS Motor Co’s scooter sales, the Apache brand is to the company’s motorcycle numbers. While the Jupiter helped power sales of a record 2.30 million scooters (up 18% YoY) in FY2026, the Apache series enabled TVS motorcycle sales to soar to a new high of 1.41 million motorcycles. Add 523,240 mopeds and TVS’ total 2W sales in FY2026 were a record 4.24 million units in FY2026, up 21% (FY2025: 3.51 million units).

As per apex industry body SIAM’s wholesales numbers for FY2026, the Apache series of motorcycles registered factory dispatches of 571,376 units, up 28% YoY (FY2025: 446,218 units). This is 21,000 units more Autocar Professional’s forecast of a record 550,000 units published in mid-December 2025. In FY2026, the Apache sold an additional 144,499 units YoY and accounted for a higher 40% model-wise share (versus 37% in FY2025) of TVS motorcycle sales.

With this highest-ever fiscal year total, the Apache has surpassed the half-a-million mark for the first time and the 400,000-units mark for the fourth time in its 21-year innings. Since launch, the Apache brand has sold nearly 7 million units including 4.38 million in the past 12 years (see data table below).

GST 2.0 rationalisation, which drove a marked fall in prices of below-350cc two-wheelers, helped accelerate Apache bike sales. While H1 FY2026 (222,048 units) saw 22% YoY growth, H2 FY2026 (223,271 units) delivered an even better 34% YoY increase.
Apache brand sales crossed half-a-million units (571,376) for the first time and contributed 40% to TVS Motor Co's record 1.41 million bikes in FY2026. The Raider 125 had a 30% model-wise share.
Along with GST 2.0, TVS Motor’s accelerated motorcycle sales were also due to the robust customer demand for the Apache series in the 150-200cc segment wherein it continues to lead the market.

2 Vehicle Manufacturer Stocks to Watch: Honda and REV Group
sum: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Two vehicle manufacturer stocks sit at opposite ends of the story spectrum. One is a global automotive giant navigating a painful EV retreat while its motorcycles quietly carry the load. The other is a specialty vehicle maker that doubled in a year before disappearing into a larger company. Here is what you need to know about both.

Honda Motor (NYSE:HMC | HMC Price Prediction) manufactures motorcycles, automobiles, and power products. Most Americans know Honda through its cars and trucks, but the motorcycle business is quietly the most important segment right now.

The headline numbers for the nine months through December 2025 are rough. Sales revenue came in at $100.39 billion, down 2.2% year-over-year. More striking, operating profit fell 48.1% to $3.72 billion, and the automobile segment swung from a $2.53 billion profit to a $1.05 billion operating loss.

The culprit is a messy EV unwind. Honda took $1.76 billion in EV-related charges during the nine-month period, covering impairments on cancelled models and onerous contract provisions tied to an alliance agreement. The company has now cut its 2030 global EV sales ratio target from 30% to 20%, a significant strategic retreat driven by slowing EV demand in North America and Europe, the end of U.S. EV tax incentives, and brutal competition from Chinese manufacturers.

Full-year FY2026 guidance tells the rest of the story. Honda now expects operating profit to fall 54.7% year-over-year and net profit to owners to drop 64.1%. Full-year EPS is guided at approximately $0.47, below the analyst consensus of $0.52.

The bright spot is motorcycles. The motorcycle segment generated $18.44 billion in revenue over nine months with growing profitability. Honda is the world’s largest motorcycle manufacturer by volume, with real pricing power in emerging markets where two-wheelers are essential transportation.

items.t: Honda reports 42% plunge on net profits in April-December 2025
sum: Japanese automaker Honda Motor Company reported a 2.2% drop in global revenues to JPY 15,975.6 billion (US$104.4 billion) in the first three quarters of the current fiscal year (FY26), between April and December 2025. The company's operating profit plunged by 48% to JPY 591.5 billion (US$ 3.9 billion), while net profit dropped by 42% to JPY 465.4 billion (US$ 304.2 billion). The company blamed the impact of US import tariffs and one-off costs relating to its US battery electric vehicle (BEV) programme for the sharp declines.

The automaker said its global vehicle sales fell by 9.1% to 2.561 million units in the nine-month period, with sales in North America falling by 4.7% to 1.211 million units, while sales in Asia (excluding Japan) fell by 18.2% to 739,000 units, and sales in Japan were down by 6.3% to 439,000 units. Revenues from vehicle sales fell by 4.3% to JPY 10,435 billion, while the automotive division made an operating loss of JPY 166.4 billion compared with an operating profit of JPY 402.6 billion previously.

Global motorcycle sales rose by 6% to 16.44 million units, while sales of power products were down slightly at 2.5 million units. Combined with financial services, these divisions made an operating profit of JPY 758 billion, more than offsetting the loss made by the automotive division.

Honda left unchanged its global revenue forecast for the full fiscal year, ending in March 2026, at JPY 21.1 trillion, representing a 2.7% decline from the previous year, while cutting its operating profit forecast to JPY 550 billion from JPY 700 billion. The company also left unchanged its global vehicle sales forecast at 3.34 million units.

Honda said it will focus on increasing the profitability of its ICE and hybrid vehicle operations, as it looks to re-establish its mid- to long-term strategy, while cutting losses associated with its US battery BEV operations.

sum: If you are considering buying the Honda Dio 125 X-Edition and wondering about the possible monthly EMIs you have to pay to own it, here is a quick and comprehensive look at the monthly EMI calculation.

Honda has recently launched the Dio 125 X-Edition scooter in the Indian market, which comes as a special edition iteration of the regular Honda Dio 125. The special edition scooter comes priced at ₹87,733 (ex-showroom). The Honda Dio 125 X-Edition comes with only a few cosmetic changes compared to the standard version of the scooter. Beyond that, it remains identical to the H-Smart variant of the regular version of Dio 125. The features, powertrain and specifications of the Honda Dio 125 X-Edition remain the same as the H-Smart trim of the Dio 125.

The Honda Dio 125 X-Edition is priced at RS 87,733 (ex-showroom). In this monthly EMI calculation, we have considered a downpayment of ₹7,733, which means your loan amount will be ₹80,000. The rates of interest considered are 8.5% and 9%, while repayment tenures considered are 12 months and 24 months.

If you opt for 8.5% rate of interest and a 12-month repayment tenure, your monthly EMI amount will be RS 6,978, which will come down to ₹3,636 if you opt for a 24-month repayment tenure. If the rate of interest increases to 9% and the repayment tenure is 12 months, the monthly EMI amount will be ₹6,996, while in the case of 24 months of repayment tenure, the EMI amount comes down to RS 3,655.

Kawasaki surges to No. 1 in the U.S. motorcycle market as Harley falls to third: Reports
sum: Kawasaki has become the top-selling motorcycle brand in the United States for 2025, overtaking both Honda and Harley-Davidson amid one of the toughest sales climates in the past decade, according to New Atlas and MotorCyclesData.

MotorCyclesData’s year-to-date figures through September show Kawasaki sales up 14.2%, the strongest performance in the industry. Honda, last year’s No. 1, slipped to second with an 8% decline. In comparison, Harley-Davidson fell to third after a steep 15.9% drop—a downturn highlighted in New Atlas reporting by Utkarsh Sood, who also cited Harley’s internal turmoil and revenue challenges as contributing factors.

Overall, the U.S. motorcycle market remains under pressure. MotorCyclesData reports 401,035 YTD sales, down 6.5% — including the worst first half in 10 years, at –9.2%. The third quarter softened slightly but remained negative at –0.5%. This compares to the Motorcycle Industry Council’s data showing the motorcycle industry is down –7.3% YTD through September.

Despite the industry slump, Kawasaki found momentum in the U.S. even as the brand struggles globally. New Atlas credits strong demand for the Ninja lineup and the Vulcan S as key drivers of its domestic surge.

Behind the top three, Yamaha held fourth (–0.4%), while KTM suffered one of the largest declines (–23.8%). Indian Motorcycle, which was recently sold to private equity, remains a bright spot, posting 4.9% growth, followed by Suzuki (–13.7%) and BMW (–10.8%).

Both reports point to a clear consumer trend: buyers are leaning toward reliable, price-competitive models from Japanese manufacturers. The entry-level pricing gap is significant — Kawasaki, Honda and Yamaha all offer sub-$5,500 models, while Harley-Davidson and Indian’s least expensive bikes start around $9,999. To that end, Harley is rumored to be working on a sub-$6,000 bike that will be released next year.

For dealers, the shifting leaderboard underscores evolving customer priorities: affordability, dependability, and value. With the U.S. market projected to remain economically constrained into 2026, brands with competitive pricing and strong small- to mid-displacement lineups appear poised to gain further share.

10 Things I Love...Toni Bou
sum: Toni Bou, the king of trial, shares the passions that fuel his extraordinary life.
It may sound obvious to say but trial riding is absolutely my biggest passion. It’s not just my profession - it’s the sport I enjoy the most and something I truly love doing every single day.

My love for motorcycles goes far beyond trial. I’m a huge MotoGP fan, and since I know many of the riders personally, following the season is even more exciting, especially when riders I consider friends achieve great results. I also enjoy motocross and supercross; this year I had the chance to attend the AMA in the United States, and it was an incredible experience.
I can’t go a day without it. I usually have at least two or three cups, always black, and I never go to a race without making sure there’s a coffee machine nearby.

I really enjoy staying active, and I’ve always preferred sports and outdoor activities over the gym. A few years ago, I started playing padel, and now I’m completely hooked - it helps me clear my mind and stay in shape at the same time.
I’ve been a Barça fan for as long as I can remember. Whenever my schedule allows, I love going to the stadium to watch the matches live - especially when I can enjoy them with friends.

Cycling is another hobby I share with my partner, Ester. When I’m home, we often go ride together on mountain passes. It’s a demanding sport, but I love the challenge and the feeling of pushing myself to the limit.
